# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1115 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1115 - **Title**: gh-1107 SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1107` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 6 - **Additions**: +810 - **Deletions**: -63 - **Created**: 2026-10-19T18:11:59Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-19T18:30:10Z ## PR Description Closes #1107 ### What changed Check-run stamps no longer interpolate run-derived text into a shell string. `stampValidationChecksForModule` now builds the Checks-API request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), writes it to a temp file, posts it with `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input `, and deletes the file in `finally`. A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; the new `--input` form posts the body byte-for-byte, and a shellQuote'd `--ref 'ai/g'\''h-50;$(touch /tmp/pwn)'` dispatch expands nothing.
Transport diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD SYNC[syncValidationChecks / validate_pr] --> STAMP[stampValidationChecksForModule] STAMP --> LB[stampLinkBlock jobs probe] LB --> BODY[checkRunStamp.buildCheckRunBody
E1: truncate summary at 65,535] BODY --> FW[file_write /tmp/sm-check-run-N.json] FW --> CLI[gh api -X POST repos/o/r/check-runs --input tmpfile
zero untrusted bytes] CLI --> DEL[file_delete in finally — success AND failure] CLI -->|throws| WARN[warn and skip — next check name] ```

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Now I understand the codebase. The CI "crap" job:
1. Runs the unit suite with nyc coverage on an instrumented tree.
2. Runs crap4js with the released baseline to compare per-function CRAP.
3. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new function exceeds threshold 8.

The failing check name is "crap". The PR added `js/common/checkRunStamp.js` with functions like `postCheckRunStamp` (try/finally with nested try/catch) and `truncateCheckRunSummary`. CRAP = Changed Risk Anti-Patterns metric: CRAP = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^100 + comp. Without coverage, even complexity 2 gives CRAP = 2^2 * 1 = 4... wait, CRAP formula: `crap = comp^2 * (1 - cov)^100 + comp` where cov is coverage ratio. With 0 coverage: comp^2 + comp. For comp=2: 4+2 = 6 > threshold 8? No, 6 < 8. For comp=3: 9+3=12 > 8.

But the tests DO cover checkRunStamp (run_checkRunStamp.json exists with UT-1..3, E1, E2). So maybe the coverage is there but CRAP still exceeds.

Actually, wait — I need to reproduce. The CI log fetch failed, so I need to run the same steps locally:

1. Install crap4js from github:IstiN/crap4js#83ee620 and nyc@17.
2. Instrument the tree.
3. Run the unit suite with coverage.
4. Fetch the baseline (needs GH_TOKEN — may be available via environment).
5. Run crap4js compare.

Let me check if dmtools is available, node version, and whether there's network access.

Let me also check the `js/unit-tests/run_all.json` to see the test list, and try running the test suite first to see if everything passes.

Actually — wait. The CI job might be failing at a different level: maybe the unit suite itself fails in the instrumented tree (the "Run the unit suite for coverage" step would fail the job). The PR description says "dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed" — that's the dmtools harness. But the quality.yml job runs the NODE harness (`node ci/run_with_coverage.js node_testRunner.js ...`). The comment in quality.yml says: "the node harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too, so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed."

So the failure might be:
1. Node harness test failure (test_smAgent.js or test_checkRunStamp.js failing under Node).
2. CRAP regression vs baseline.

The check name "crap" is the job name — any step failure shows as job "crap" failure.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1115 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1115 - **Title**: gh-1107 SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1107` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 6 - **Additions**: +810 - **Deletions**: -63 - **Created**: 2026-10-19T18:11:59Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-19T18:30:10Z ## PR Description Closes #1107 ### What changed Check-run stamps no longer interpolate run-derived text into a shell string. `stampValidationChecksForModule` now builds the Checks-API request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), writes it to a temp file, posts it with `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input `, and deletes the file in `finally`. A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; the new `--input` form posts the body byte-for-byte, and a shellQuote'd `--ref 'ai/g'\''h-50;$(touch /tmp/pwn)'` dispatch expands nothing.
Transport diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD SYNC[syncValidationChecks / validate_pr] --> STAMP[stampValidationChecksForModule] STAMP --> LB[stampLinkBlock jobs probe] LB --> BODY[checkRunStamp.buildCheckRunBody
E1: truncate summary at 65,535] BODY --> FW[file_write /tmp/sm-check-run-N.json] FW --> CLI[gh api -X POST repos/o/r/check-runs --input tmpfile
zero untrusted bytes] CLI --> DEL[file_delete in finally — success AND failure] CLI -->|throws| WARN[warn and skip — next check name] ```

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Already-addressed / invalid threads (gh-957 audit-resolve) The thread list in `pr_discussions.md` / `pr_discussions_raw.json` comes from the SAME GraphQL reviewThreads census the SM armer counts (gh-957) — if it lists threads, they are really open on GitHub and each one needs exactly one reply entry in `outputs/review_replies.json`. A reply entry does NOT always imply a code commit: - **Already addressed** — verify against the current head; cite the commit/file/line that covers the finding. - **Invalid finding** — explain precisely why it does not apply to this code. When every open thread has a targeted reply and the pass pushed no commits, the post-action resolves the threads with an explanatory audit line (rework run URL) per thread — this is the ONLY permitted resolution-without-changes path. Partial coverage resolves NOTHING: the pass is reported blocked. Never leave an open thread without a reply entry. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check …

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1115 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1115 - **Title**: gh-1107 SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1107` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 6 - **Additions**: +810 - **Deletions**: -63 - **Created**: 2026-10-19T18:11:59Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-19T18:30:10Z ## PR Description Closes #1107 ### What changed Check-run stamps no longer interpolate run-derived text into a shell string. `stampValidationChecksForModule` now builds the Checks-API request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), writes it to a temp file, posts it with `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input `, and deletes the file in `finally`. A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; the new `--input` form posts the body byte-for-byte, and a shellQuote'd `--ref 'ai/g'\''h-50;$(touch /tmp/pwn)'` dispatch expands nothing.
Transport diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD SYNC[syncValidationChecks / validate_pr] --> STAMP[stampValidationChecksForModule] STAMP --> LB[stampLinkBlock jobs probe] LB --> BODY[checkRunStamp.buildCheckRunBody
E1: truncate summary at 65,535] BODY --> FW[file_write /tmp/sm-check-run-N.json] FW --> CLI[gh api -X POST repos/o/r/check-runs --input tmpfile
zero untrusted bytes] CLI --> DEL[file_delete in finally — success AND failure] CLI -->|throws| WARN[warn and skip — next check name] ```

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1115 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents/pull/1115 - **Title**: gh-1107 SM: check-run stamps fail with 'Bad substitution' — job names interpolated into shell string - **Author**: dmtools-factory-bot[bot] - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1107` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 6 - **Additions**: +810 - **Deletions**: -63 - **Created**: 2026-10-19T18:11:59Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-19T18:30:10Z ## PR Description Closes #1107 ### What changed Check-run stamps no longer interpolate run-derived text into a shell string. `stampValidationChecksForModule` now builds the Checks-API request body as JSON (`{name, head_sha, status, conclusion?, details_url?, output:{title, summary}}`), writes it to a temp file, posts it with `gh api -X POST repos/{o}/{r}/check-runs --input `, and deletes the file in `finally`. A job named `Lockfile smoke (${{ matrix.os }} release)` therefore reaches dash only as JSON payload bytes — the command string carries zero untrusted bytes, so `Bad substitution` (exit 2, missing stamps, blocked PRs) cannot recur. Transport + helpers live in a new `js/common/checkRunStamp.js`. ### Key decisions - Temp-file JSON body (`--input`) instead of escaping: JSON preserves `${{ }}`, `$(id)`, backticks, `"`, `\`, newlines byte-for-byte (AC1); the same gh-960 PR-body precedent `scm.js` already uses. Only the fixed repo path and a digits-only `/tmp/sm-check-run--.json` path ever touch the shell (AC2). - Temp file deleted in `finally` — on success AND failure (AC3); an unwritable temp dir warns and skips exactly like the old failure mode (E2); summary > 65,535 chars truncates with a marker, never rejected (E1). - `stampLinkBlock` dropped its legacy `"` → `'` mangling — the body must be byte-for-byte, and quotes are safe inside JSON. - AC5 audit of `cli_execute_command` sites interpolating PR/run-derived text — all converted through ONE `shellQuote` (re-exported from `factory/token_usage.js` via `checkRunStamp.js`): - `dispatchCiWorkflow` `--ref ` (validate-arm CI dispatch) — was bare unquoted; - silent-update chain (classic): `--branch ` + push refspec — was bare; - silent-update chain (fork, gh-1070): `git checkout -B ` + `HEAD:` refspec — was bare; - gh-757 ghost dispatch — inline `'`-escaping normalized to the shared helper (byte-identical output); - gh-857 placeholder conclusion PATCH — `details_url` (run-derived URL) + `output[summary]` values now shellQuote'd; - gh-998 zombie-sweep PATCH — fixed-literal summary moved to the same helper so the shape cannot regress. - Audited and left as-is (no untrusted bytes): probe calls keyed on config `ciWorkflow`, hex head SHAs, numeric run/check-run ids; local-teammate runner (Jira key + config values); factory-state transport (already shellQuote'd); zombie/gh-848 PATCH summaries (fixed literals); stderr-file paths (sanitized at creation). - DRY path unchanged (AC4): same `[dry] stamp …` log, no file, no command. ### How to verify ```bash dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json # stamp + hostile-string pins dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_checkRunStamp.json # transport unit tests (UT-1..3, E1, E2) dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json # full suite: 4760 passed, 0 failed ``` Real-shell spot check (reproduces the live bug and proves the fix): the old `-f summary="…(${{ matrix.os }})…"` form exits 2 with `Bad substitution` under dash; the new `--input` form posts the body byte-for-byte, and a shellQuote'd `--ref 'ai/g'\''h-50;$(touch /tmp/pwn)'` dispatch expands nothing.

E1: truncate summary at 65,535] BODY --> FW[file_write /tmp/sm-check-run-N.json] FW --> CLI[gh api -X POST repos/o/r/check-runs --input tmpfile
zero untrusted bytes] CLI --> DEL[file_delete in finally — success AND failure] CLI -->|throws| WARN[warn and skip — next check name] ```
